The content already ends with a line ending.\n        return block.content\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n\nclass ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The document-wide map from normalized label to definition. The first definition wins.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self._entries: dict[str, LinkReference] = {}\n\n    def add(self, label: str, destination: str, title: str | None = None) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Store a definition under its normalized label unless that label is already present.\"\"\"\n        key = normalize_label(label)\n        if key not in self._entries:\n            self._entries[key] = LinkReference(destination, title)\n\n    def get(self, label: str) -> LinkReference | None:\n        \"\"\"The definition for `label`, matched on its normalized form, or None when absent.\"\"\"\n        return self._entries.get(normalize_label(label))\n\n    def __contains__(self, label: object) -> bool:\n        return isinstance(label, str) and normalize_label(label) in self._entries\n\n    def __len__(self) -> int:\n        return len(self._entries)\n\n\ndef extract_definitions(text: str, references: ReferenceMap) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove the link reference definitions at the start of a closed paragraph's text.\n\n    Each definition found is added to `references`. Scanning stops at the first line that is not a\n    definition, and the rest of the text is returned. Text that is not at the start of the\n    paragraph is never examined, so a definition cannot interrupt a paragraph.\n    \"\"\"\n    pos = 0\n    while pos < len(text):\n        parsed = _parse_definition(text, pos)\n        if parsed is None:\n            break\n        label, destination, title, pos = parsed\n        references.add(label, destination, title)\n    return text[pos:]\n\n\n\"\"\"ATX heading tests: the six declared checks from FEATURE-ATX-Headings.md, then block-tree and\nexact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import ATX_HEADING, INDENTED_CODE, PARAGRAPH, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, source: str) -> str:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks opening-sequence length from 1 to 6 renders exactly one heading of that level.\"\"\"\n    source = \"#\" * level + \" foo\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\" + str(level) + \">\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_atx_not_a_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Seven hashes, a missing space, and an escaped hash do not produce headings.\"\"\"\n    source = \"####### foo\\n\\n#hashtag\\n\\n\\\\## foo\\n\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 3\n\n\ndef test_atx_closing_sequence(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A closing hash sequence is removed from the heading content.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"## foo ##\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"#\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_atx_empty_heading(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Empty headings are allowed, one per line.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"#\\n\\n##\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_atx_interrupts_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A heading splits a paragraph without blank lines, leaving two paragraphs around it.\"\"\"\n    result = {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0126XizZcojBVdGWFKv2nbfj","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"4d711a92-86bf-4dac-abf0-e12560b81234","uuid":"e09109d9-6aae-4d8a-ae59-2a58c17da3ab","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:58:31.066Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py","oldString":"DOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(","newString":"SETEXT_MAX_INDENT = 3\nSETEXT_LEVELS = {\"=\": 1, \"-\": 2}\n\n\ndef _setext_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Turn the open paragraph into a setext heading when the line is an underline of `=` or `-`.\n\n    The underline has up to three spaces of indentation, one run of a single marker character and\n    only trailing spaces or tabs after it. It applies to the whole paragraph, so every paragraph line\n    becomes heading content. Definitions at the start of the paragraph are extracted first; if nothing\n    is left, the line is not an underline and the paragraph keeps it as text.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind is not PARAGRAPH or cursor.indent > SETEXT_MAX_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    marker = line[start : start + 1]\n    if marker not in SETEXT_LEVELS:\n        return None\n    underline = line[start:].rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if underline.count(marker) != len(underline):\n        return None\n    text = \"\\n\".join(container.lines).strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(container))\n    if not content:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    # The paragraph's text now lives in the heading. Clearing its lines lets the paragraph close\n    # empty, so it leaves the tree and the heading takes its place.\n    container.lines = []\n    heading = Block(SETEXT_HEADING)\n    heading.level = SETEXT_LEVELS[marker]\n    heading.content = content\n    return heading\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(","newString":"# A setext heading is a complete block made from the open paragraph. Its content is parsed as inlines\n# when the document is rendered, like an ATX heading.\nSETEXT_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"setext_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_setext_heading_start,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() Its start rule, if any, joins the start rules in order.\"\"\"\n        if block_type.name in self._names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type already registered: {block_type.name!r}\")\n        self._names.add(block_type.name)\n        if block_type.start is not None:\n            self._starts.append(block_type)\n\n    def starts(self) -> tuple[BlockType, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The registered block types that have a start rule, in registration order.\"\"\"\n        return tuple(self._starts)\n\n\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(THEMATIC_BREAK)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(ATX_HEADING)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(INDENTED_CODE)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(FENCED_CODE)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(HTML_BLOCK)\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(BLOCK_QUOTE)\n\n\nclass DocumentParser:\n    \"\"\"Runs the phase 1 per-line procedure over a document, one line at a time.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry\n        self.root = Block(registry.root)\n        self.root.references = ReferenceMap()\n\n    def incorporate_line(self, line: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Match open blocks, look for new starts, then add the remaining text.\"\"\"\n        cursor = Cursor(line)\n\n        # 1. Match open blocks. Unmatched blocks stay open: the line may be a lazy continuation.\n        container = self._match_open_blocks(cursor)\n        all_closed = container.open_last_child() is None\n\n        # 2. Look for new block starts. Unmatched blocks are closed only once a start succeeds. A line that\n        # can only lazily continue the open paragraph may start only a block that can interrupt one.\n        cursor.lazy_paragraph = not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and self._tip().kind.lazy\n        started = False\n        while not self._is_text_leaf(container):\n            new_block = self._try_starts(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is None:\n                break\n            if not started:\n                started = True\n                all_closed = True\n                cursor.lazy_paragraph = False\n                self._close_below(container)\n            self._attach(new_block, container)\n            container = new_block\n\n        # 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n            return\n        self._close_below(container)\n        if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n            self._add_line(container, cursor)\n        elif not cursor.is_blank():\n            paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n            self._attach(paragraph, container)\n            self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n\n    def finish(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"Close every open block and return the document root.\"\"\"\n        self._close_below(self.root)\n        self.root.is_open = False\n        return self.root\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:\n        container = self.root\n        while True:\n            child = container.open_last_child()\n            if child is None or not child.kind.continues(child, cursor):\n                return container\n            container = child\n\n    def _try_starts(self, cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n        for block_type in self.registry.starts():\n            assert block_type.start is not None\n            new_block = block_type.start(cursor, container)\n            if new_block is not None:\n                return new_block\n        return None\n\n    def _is_text_leaf(self, block: Block) -> bool:\n        return block.kind.accepts_lines and not block.kind.interruptible\n\n    def _attach(self, new_block: Block, container: Block) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add `new_block` under `container`, closing any leaf that cannot hold it.\"\"\"\n        while not container.kind.is_container:\n            self._finalize(container)\n            assert container.parent is not None\n            container = container.parent\n        container.children.append(new_block)\n        new_block.parent = container\n\n    def _add_line(self, block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n        assert block.kind.add_line is not None\n        block.kind.add_line(block, cursor)\n\n    def _tip(self) -> Block:\n        \"\"\"The deepest open block.\"\"\"\n block.is_open = False\n        if block.kind.finalize is not None:\n            block.kind.finalize(block)\n\n\ndef parse_lines(lines: Iterable[str], registry: BlockRegistry = DEFAULT_REGISTRY) -> Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nSETEXT_MAX_INDENT = 3\nSETEXT_LEVELS = {\"=\": 1, \"-\": 2}\n\n\ndef _setext_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Turn the open paragraph into a setext heading when the line is an underline of `=` or `-`.\n\n    The underline has up to three spaces of indentation, one run of a single marker character and\n    only trailing spaces or tabs after it. It applies to the whole paragraph, so every paragraph line\n    becomes heading content. Definitions at the start of the paragraph are extracted first; if nothing\n    is left, the line is not an underline and the paragraph keeps it as text.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind is not PARAGRAPH or cursor.indent > SETEXT_MAX_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    marker = line[start : start + 1]\n    if marker not in SETEXT_LEVELS:\n        return None\n    underline = line[start:].rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if underline.count(marker) != len(underline):\n        return None\n    text = \"\\n\".join(container.lines).strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(container))\n    if not content:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    # The paragraph's text now lives in the heading. Clearing its lines lets the paragraph close\n    # empty, so it leaves the tree and the heading takes its place.\n    container.lines = []\n    heading = Block(SETEXT_HEADING)\n    heading.level = SETEXT_LEVELS[marker]\n    heading.content = content\n    return heading\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A setext heading is a complete block made from the open paragraph. Its content is parsed as inlines\n# when the document is rendered, like an ATX heading.\nSETEXT_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"setext_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_setext_heading_start,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph. The same holds\n    for a lazy continuation of a paragraph that an unmatched container holds.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.lazy_paragraph or cursor.is_blank():\n        return None\n    if cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\nFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\nBACKTICK = \"`\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n\n    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    indent: int\n    language: str\n    opening: bool = True\n    closed: bool = False\n\n\ndef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _language(info: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n\n    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.\n    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the\n    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    char = line[start]\n    end = _run_end(line, start, char)\n    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:\n        return None\n    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:\n        return None\n    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)\n    block.fence = fence\n    return block\n\n\ndef _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.\n\n    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three\n    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return False\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)\n    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.\n\n    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening\n    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n    \"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.closed:\n        return False\n    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n        fence.closed = True\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return True\n    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n    return True\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_014asifSbm7JxuSUSh17gYoh","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"4d711a92-86bf-4dac-abf0-e12560b81234","uuid":"4b66dc4f-b2ca-490b-8b79-c88028b29e38","timestamp":"2026-10-14T07:58:33.744Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/render.py","oldString":"    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":","newString":"    if block.kind.name in (\"atx_heading\", \"setext_heading\"):","originalFile":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return _render_children(root, parse_inline)\n\n\ndef _render_children(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in block.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"block_quote\":\n        return f\"<blockquote>\\n{_render_children(block, parse_inline)}</blockquote>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"html_block\":\n        # Raw lines pass through unchanged. The content already ends with a line ending.\n        return block.content\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":72,"oldLines":7,"newStart":72,"newLines":7,"lines":["         return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"","     if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":","         return \"<hr />\\n\"","-    if block.kind.name == \"atx_heading\":","+    if block.kind.name in (\"atx_heading\", \"setext_heading\"):","         return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"","     if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":","         return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\""]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_014asifSbm7JxuSUSh17gYoh","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1mtduew4Wfi9FBuCYcx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013bPCUiFMuVnXQkjQiSG8BW","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_setext_headings.py","content":"\"\"\"Setext heading tests: the seven declared checks from FEATURE-Setext-Headings.md, then block-tree and\nexact-output tests through the `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import PARAGRAPH, SETEXT_HEADING, THEMATIC_BREAK, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, source: str) -> str:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Setext-Headings.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_setext_both_levels(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Equals underlines give h1 and dash underlines give h2.\"\"\"\n    equals = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n=========\\n\")\n    dashes = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n---------\\n\")\n    print(equals.stdout)\n    print(dashes.stdout)\n    assert equals.returncode == 0\n    assert dashes.returncode == 0\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert dashes.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_multiline_content(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Several paragraph lines before the underline become one heading with no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\nBar\\n---\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_beats_thematic_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes after paragraph text make a heading, not a thematic break.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n---\\nbar\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_sequence_with_thematic_breaks(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes with no preceding paragraph are thematic breaks, mixed with two setext headings and a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"---\\nFoo\\n---\\nBar\\n---\\nBaz\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_limits(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four spaces of indentation or internal spaces disqualify the underline.\"\"\"\n    for source in (\"Foo\\n    ---\\n\", \"Foo\\n= =\\n\"):\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_not_lazy_in_quote(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unmarked underline after a quote paragraph does not make a heading inside the quote.\"\"\"\n    result = kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in result.stdout\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Setext-Headings.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_setext_both_levels(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Equals underlines give h1 and dash underlines give h2.\"\"\"\n    equals = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n=========\\n\")\n    dashes = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n---------\\n\")\n    print(equals.stdout)\n    print(dashes.stdout)\n    assert equals.returncode == 0\n    assert dashes.returncode == 0\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert dashes.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_multiline_content(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Several paragraph lines before the underline become one heading with no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\nBar\\n---\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_beats_thematic_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes after paragraph text make a heading, not a thematic break.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n---\\nbar\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_sequence_with_thematic_breaks(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes with no preceding paragraph are thematic breaks, mixed with two setext headings and a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"---\\nFoo\\n---\\nBar\\n---\\nBaz\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_limits(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four spaces of indentation or internal spaces disqualify the underline.\"\"\"\n    for source in (\"Foo\\n    ---\\n\", \"Foo\\n= =\\n\"):\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef mdparser.blocks import PARAGRAPH, SETEXT_HEADING, THEMATIC_BREAK, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return result.stdout\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Setext-Headings.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_setext_both_levels(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Equals underlines give h1 and dash underlines give h2.\"\"\"\n    equals = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n=========\\n\")\n    dashes = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n---------\\n\")\n    print(equals.stdout)\n    print(dashes.stdout)\n    assert equals.returncode == 0\n    assert dashes.returncode == 0\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert dashes.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_multiline_content(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Several paragraph lines before the underline become one heading with no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\nBar\\n---\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_beats_thematic_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes after paragraph text make a heading, not a thematic break.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n---\\nbar\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_sequence_with_thematic_breaks(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes with no preceding paragraph are thematic breaks, mixed with two setext headings and a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"---\\nFoo\\n---\\nBar\\n---\\nBaz\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_limits(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four spaces of indentation or internal spaces disqualify the underline.\"\"\"\n    for source in (\"Foo\\n    ---\\n\", \"Foo\\n= =\\n\"):\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_not_lazy_in_quote(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unmarked underline after a quote paragraph does not make a heading inside the quote.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\nbar\\n===\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_quote_then_thematic_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes after a quote without a marker are a thematic break outside the quote.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> Foo\\n---\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert -> None:\n    \"\"\"An underline with no content line is not a heading.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n====\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Block tree: underline levels and shape ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize((\"marker\", \"level\"), ===\"\n\n\ndef test_internal_space_in_underline_is_paragraph_text() -> None:\n    (block,) = parse_lines([\"Foo\", \"= =\"]).children\n    assert block.kind is PARAGRAPH\n\n\ndef kinds([\"Foo\", \"-=-\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\n# --- Block tree: precedence over thematic break ---\n\n\ndef test_dashes_after_paragraph_are_not_a_thematic_break() -> None:\n    assert neighbours and continuation ---\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_resumes_after_setext_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"===\", \"bar\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name, PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_setext_heading_followed_by_blank_line_stays_one_block() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"===\", \"\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_before_setext_heading_is_replaced_not_kept() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"Bar\", \"===\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_text_after_underline_line_opens_a_new_paragraph() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"===\", \"Bar\", \"===\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name, SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_heading_inside_quote_when_underline_is_marked() -> None:\n    (quote,) = parse_lines([\"> Foo\", \"> ===\"]).children\n    assert quote.kind.name == \"block_quote\"\n    assert [child.kind.name for child in quote.children] == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_link_definition_is_not_heading_text() -> None:\n    (block,) = parse_lines([\"[foo]: /url\", \"Bar\", \"===\"]).children\n    assert The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import PARAGRAPH, SETEXT_HEADING, THEMATIC_BREAK, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, source: str) -> str:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Setext-Headings.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_setext_both_levels(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Equals underlines give h1 and dash underlines give h2.\"\"\"\n    equals = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n=========\\n\")\n    dashes = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n---------\\n\")\n    print(equals.stdout)\n    print(dashes.stdout)\n    assert equals.returncode == 0\n    assert dashes.returncode == 0\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert dashes.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_multiline_content(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Several paragraph lines before the underline become one heading with no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\nBar\\n---\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_beats_thematic_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes after paragraph text make a heading, not a thematic break.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n---\\nbar\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_sequence_with_thematic_breaks(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes with no preceding paragraph are thematic breaks, mixed with two setext headings and a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"---\\nFoo\\n---\\nBar\\n---\\nBaz\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_limits(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four spaces of indentation or internal spaces disqualify the underline.\"\"\"\n    for source in (\"Foo\\n    ---\\n\", \"Foo\\n= =\\n\"):\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_not_lazy_in_quote(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unmarked underline after a quote paragraph does not make a heading inside the quote.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\nbar\\n===\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_quote_then_thematic_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes after a quote without a marker are a thematic break outside the quote.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> Foo\\n---\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_setext_empty_is_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An underline with no content line is not a heading.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n====\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Block tree: underline levels and shape ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize((\"marker\", \"level\"), neighbours and continuation ---\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_resumes_after_setext_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"===\", \"bar\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name, PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_setext_heading_followed_by_blank_line_stays_one_block() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"===\", \"\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_before_setext_heading_is_replaced_not_kept() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"Bar\", \"===\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import PARAGRAPH, SETEXT_HEADING, THEMATIC_BREAK, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the top-level block types that `lines` produce, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in parse_lines(lines).children]\n\n\ndef render(project_root: Path, source: str) -> str:\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    return result.stdout\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-Setext-Headings.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_setext_both_levels(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Equals underlines give h1 and dash underlines give h2.\"\"\"\n    equals = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n=========\\n\")\n    dashes = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo *bar*\\n---------\\n\")\n    print(equals.stdout)\n    print(dashes.stdout)\n    assert equals.returncode == 0\n    assert dashes.returncode == 0\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert dashes.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<em>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_multiline_content(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Several paragraph lines before the underline become one heading with no paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\nBar\\n---\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_beats_thematic_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes after paragraph text make a heading, not a thematic break.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"Foo\\n---\\nbar\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_sequence_with_thematic_breaks(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes with no preceding paragraph are thematic breaks, mixed with two setext headings and a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"---\\nFoo\\n---\\nBar\\n---\\nBaz\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 2\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_underline_limits(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Four spaces of indentation or internal spaces disqualify the underline.\"\"\"\n    for source in (\"Foo\\n    ---\\n\", \"Foo\\n= =\\n\"):\n        result = run_commonmark(project_root, source)\n        print(result.stdout)\n        assert result.returncode == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 0\n        assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_not_lazy_in_quote(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unmarked underline after a quote paragraph does not make a heading inside the quote.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> foo\\nbar\\n===\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_setext_quote_then_thematic_break(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dashes after a quote without a marker are a thematic break outside the quote.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"> Foo\\n---\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<blockquote>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<hr />\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h2>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_setext_empty_is_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An underline with no content line is not a heading.\"\"\"\n    result = run_commonmark(project_root, \"\\n====\\n\")\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Block tree: underline levels and shape ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize((\"marker\", \"level\"), [(\"=\", 1), (\"-\", 2)])\ndef test_underline_run_makes_setext_heading_at_its_level(marker: str, level: int) -> None:\n    (block,) = parse_lines([\"Foo\", marker * 3]).children\n    assert block.kind is SETEXT_HEADING\n    assert block.level == level\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"length\", [1, 2, 9])\ndef test_underline_of_any_length_is_a_heading(length: int) -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"=\" * length]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_heading_content_is_all_paragraph_lines_joined() -> None:\n    (block,) = parse_lines([\"Foo\", \"Bar\", \"---\"]).children\n    assert test_up_to_three_spaces_before_underline(indent: int) -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \" \" * indent + \"===\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef ===\"\n\n\ndef test_internal_space_in_underline_is_paragraph_text() -> None:\n    (block,) = parse_lines([\"Foo\", \"= =\"]).children\n    assert block.kind is PARAGRAPH\n\n\ndef kinds([\"Foo\", \"-=-\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\n# --- Block tree: precedence over thematic break ---\n\n\ndef test_dashes_after_paragraph_are_not_a_thematic_break() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"---\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_dashes_without_paragraph_are_a_thematic_break() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"---\"]) == [THEMATIC_BREAK.name]\n\n\ndef test_asterisks_after_paragraph_are_a_thematic_break() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"***\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name, THEMATIC_BREAK.name]\n\n\ndef test_underscores_after_paragraph_are_a_thematic_break() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"___\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name, THEMATIC_BREAK.name]\n\n\ndef test_equals_alone_is_paragraph_text() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"====\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_empty_setext_heading_is_never_produced() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"\", \"====\"]) == [PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\n# --- Block tree: neighbours and continuation ---\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_resumes_after_setext_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"===\", \"bar\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name, PARAGRAPH.name]\n\n\ndef test_setext_heading_followed_by_blank_line_stays_one_block() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"===\", \"\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_before_setext_heading_is_replaced_not_kept() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"Bar\", \"===\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_second_underline_after_new_paragraph_makes_second_heading() -> None:\n    assert kinds([\"Foo\", \"===\", \"Bar\", \"===\"]) == [SETEXT_HEADING.name, SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef for child in quote.children] == [SETEXT_HEADING.name]\n\n\ndef test_link_definition_is_not_heading_text() -> None:\n    (block,) = parse_lines([\"[foo]: /url\", \"Bar\", \"===\"]).children\n    assert
